Real estate CRM

Two buyers, one flat, never.

A CRM for Indian developers that runs the line from enquiry to booking: leads tagged by source including the NRI desk and channel partners, six pipeline stages with an age on every card, site visits, holds that name a buyer and expire on a clock, and a booking that takes the unit off the market the instant it exists. It files nothing with a RERA authority — the registration number sits on the project and prints on your documents, and there is no portal connection behind it.

Where the leads come from, and why source is a field

Source is not a note somebody types. It changes what happens next, what the lead is worth, and who gets paid.

  • Portals

    High volume, low intent, decays in hours. Needs an owner in seconds and a call the same day, which is a different service level from a walk-in.

  • Walk-ins and hoardings

    Already at the location and already interested. Logged at the site, not typed up at night from a register nobody can read, because the follow-up window is that evening.

  • Channel partners

    The lead carries the partner, so brokerage on the eventual booking and the tax deducted on it come from one record instead of two spreadsheets that disagree at quarter end.

  • The NRI desk

    Separate because the next step is not a site visit. It is a video walkthrough in their evening, documents attested differently, and payment from an NRE or NRO account. In the general queue these go quiet.

Six stages, and what each is actually for

Rename them to match how your team talks. What matters is that a card cannot sit between two of them.

  1. New enquiry

    Captured, de-duplicated on phone number, assigned by rule. The measure is time to first contact in minutes, and it is the one pipeline number a developer can improve this week.

  2. Qualified

    Budget, configuration, timeline, and whether they are buying to live in or to let. A two-bedroom enquiry against four-bedroom inventory is a lead to close politely, not nurture for six months.

  3. Site visit scheduled

    A date, a time, and the person meeting them. This is where the pipeline leaks most, because a visit agreed on a call and never written down does not happen.

  4. Site visit done

    What they saw, which unit they liked, and the objection they raised. The objection is the field everyone skips and the one that decides the next call.

  5. Negotiation

    Price, payment plan, and the specific concession being argued about. A hold usually starts here, which is where the clock begins to matter.

  6. Booked

    The unit changes state and leaves availability. Everything after this is collections against the demand schedule.

Holds, bookings, and the race two salespeople will eventually run

A hold names a buyer and carries an expiry timestamp. Not a colour on a chart, and not an understanding between two people. Expired holds are swept the moment the board loads, because a hold that lapsed on Friday and still reads as held on Monday is a flat you could have sold over the weekend.

What a hold is not is a sale. It creates no obligation and does not take the unit off the market — only a booking does that, and the booking is what changes the unit's state, so a second attempt on the same unit is refused with the unit named rather than accepted by a screen that had not refreshed. Two salespeople on two phones in two corners of the office is not a rare edge case. It is a Saturday, and it is the most expensive thing a spreadsheet-run sales team does.

Held, blocked and booked also mean three different things to a lender and to a board, and collapsing them into unsold is how a healthy project reads as a failing one.

Site visits, because the ratio is the whole business

Leads are cheap to count and mean little. Visits are expensive, countable and predictive.

  • A source producing 300 enquiries and 4 visits and a source producing 40 enquiries and 22 visits are not comparable on any lead-based number. Conversion is measured on visits.
  • The unit shown is recorded against the visit, so a configuration shown constantly and never booked is pricing information months before a quarterly review.

Construction-linked demands

A construction-linked plan raises the demand when a milestone is certified, not on a calendar date. The third column is what happens when the trigger is a person remembering.

TriggerWhat is raisedWhat goes wrong without it
BookingBooking amountCollected but never recorded against the unit's schedule
Agreement and registrationThe agreement instalmentRegistration proceeds with money outstanding and nobody notices for a quarter
Each slab certifiedOne instalment per slabTwelve slabs and eleven demands is a gap found at handover
Possession offeredFinal instalment and duesKeys handed over against an unreconciled balance

RERA, absorption, and the numbers a board asks for

What the software does about each. Filing is not on this list, deliberately.

  • The RERA registration number sits on the project and prints where it must. No connection to any state authority's portal, no quarterly upload, nothing submitted on your behalf.
  • Delay interest is symmetric under the Act: the rate you charge a late buyer is the rate you owe a buyer you delayed. The agreement rate is compared against it and a divergence is flagged, because only one of the two survives a dispute.
  • Seventy percent of collections belong in the designated account. We do not operate your escrow, and the collection data is in a shape you can reconcile the transfer against.
  • Absorption excludes units that were never on the market. A 240-unit project with 40 held for promoters and 120 sold is 60 percent absorbed, not 50, and that difference is a whole conversation with a lender.

What it does not do for a developer

The gap between what a demo shows and what a project needs is where these implementations go wrong. So, before the demo.

  • No RERA portal filing of any kind. The data is in a state you can file from. A person files. No sub-registrar integration either.
  • No drawings, no BIM, no CAD, no labour attendance at the gate, no critical-path scheduling. Milestones and certification, yes. Primavera, no.
  • No payment gateway for collecting demands. Receipts are entered by hand, though a bounced cheque does release the allocation and recompute interest from the original due date.
  • No polished buyer app. A portal capability exists and we will not sell it to you as a customer experience.

Questions people actually ask

Our sales team lives on WhatsApp. Will they use this?

Only if it is faster than what they do now, on a phone, standing at a site. So the first version is deliberately small: capture, assign, log the visit, set the next date. Reporting comes after people are in it daily, never before.

Can we run four projects at once?

Yes, with inventory, demands and absorption per project and one pipeline your team works from. Consolidating several legal entities into one set of books is a different requirement and not one we serve.

Tell us how a flat gets sold in your office today.

Who takes the call, where the availability list lives, and what happens when two people sell the same unit. That answers more than a feature list.
